issues.legal_issue: Amended tenant-protection provisions govern the disposal of an ejectment suit that remains pending when the amendments take effect, and an incomplete proceeding under the former scheme must yield to the amended scheme.
material_facts: An ejectment suit was pending when the tenant-protection law was extended to the area, and the tenant applied for an order requiring the landlord to sell the site.
Before the later amendments took effect, a court declared the tenant entitled to purchase the site and directed that its value be determined, but no final order directing conveyance was made.
The amendments changed the purchase scheme and expressly made the amended provisions applicable to pending suits and proceedings.
The proceeding remained incomplete when the amendments took effect.
issues.conclusion: The amended provisions governed disposal of the pending suit. The earlier order did not conclude the proceeding; it stood superseded, and the court had to proceed under the amended scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 9 and 10 of the Madras City Tenants’ Protection Act, 1921, as amended by Madras Act XIII of 1960, made the amended scheme applicable to pending ejectment suits and proceedings. The amended section 9 altered the extent of land that could be purchased and the method of determining its price. Under the original section 9(3), the proceeding was not concluded until the court, after payment of the price, directed conveyance. The Court also relied on Gnanaprakasam and Another v. Mahboob Bi and others for the proposition that an application was not at an end before final orders directing conveyance and delivery of possession.

predicates.ejectment_case_pending_when_amendment_to: A landlord’s ejectment suit or related proceeding remained pending when the amending law took effect.
predicates.amendment_applied_new_procedure_to_pendi: The amending law provided that its new procedure applied to pending suits or proceedings.
predicates.tenant_purchase_proceeding_not_finalized: The court had not yet made the final order directing conveyance after the tenant paid the price.

issues.definition: When an ejectment case remains pending at the time a law makes a new procedure applicable to pending cases, and the tenant’s purchase proceeding has not been finalized, the new procedure governs that case.

issues.legal_issue: A party may seek relief under amended provisions in the court below after an earlier appeal has ended when that appeal was confined to the validity of the former provisions and did not consider the amendments.
material_facts: An appeal to the Supreme Court concerned the validity of the former statutory provisions.
The Supreme Court confined its consideration to that validity issue and declined to consider the effect of amendments made while the appeal was pending.
After the appeal was disposed of, a party applied to the court below for relief under the amended provisions.
issues.conclusion: The party was entitled to apply to the court below for relief under the amended provisions after the earlier appeal had been disposed of.
issues.legal_principle: The scope of the earlier appeal was limited to the validity of sections 9 and 12 of the unamended Madras City Tenants’ Protection Act, and the Supreme Court declined to consider the operation of the 1960 amendments. Because the amended provisions were not within the scope of that appeal, seeking relief under them in the court below after the appeal ended was not barred by the earlier appeal’s disposal.

predicates.appeal_concerning_validity_of_former_pro: A party appealed in a proceeding that concerned the validity of the law as it stood before amendment.
predicates.appeal_scope_excluded_later_amendments: The appeal did not consider the effect or operation of amendments made while it was pending.
predicates.application_made_after_appeal_disposed: A party sought relief under the amended law in the court below after the appeal had been disposed of.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns only the validity of former provisions, excludes later amendments from its scope, and a party applies under those amendments after the appeal ends, the later application is permitted.
